instruction: I want to speed up my downloads in Chrome. Can you enable the 'enable-parallel-downloading' experiment flag?

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling parallel downloading experiment to speed up downloads. Uses existing evaluator functions.
metadata.verification: Reuses existing evaluator functions from chrome.py.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL LOGIC ERROR in metric check_enabled_experiments (chrome.py:533): Uses exact list equality comparison (==) instead of membership/subset check
The metric logic 'return 1. if enabled_experiments_names == rule['names'] else 0.' will FAIL if user has ANY other Chrome experiments enabled besides the target

Example failure scenario: If user already has ['some-other-flag'] enabled, after enabling 'enable-parallel-downloading' the list becomes ['enable-parallel-downloading', 'some-other-flag'], which != ['enable-parallel-downloading'], causing verification to fail
The instruction only requires ENABLING 'enable-parallel-downloading', not ensuring ONLY that flag is enabled (no other experiments). The metric is overly restrictive.
Semantic verification adequacy: The evaluator CANNOT correctly verify the instruction because it will produce false negatives when other experiments are present
This is a fundamental logic flaw, not just an edge case - it will fail in any realistic Chrome environment where users have customized their browser
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change metric from exact equality to membership check: 'return 1. if 'enable-parallel-downloading' in enabled_experiments_names else 0.'
Better solution (handles multiple target experiments): 'return 1. if set(rule['names']).issubset(set(enabled_experiments_names)) else 0.'
This checks if ALL required experiments from rule['names'] are present in enabled_experiments_names, without requiring they are the ONLY experiments enabled
